CHIEF CORRECTION TO AN OVERSTATED CLAIM. Previously recorded: AuthorizedRemoteRequest's Scaladoc guarantee "no code path can hand raw text to a remote provider" is false because fromProduct mints one with any payload. THAT IS WRONG. The type IS forgeable (case class, private[embed] constructor, Mirror present), but its payload field is typed PseudonymizedText, which is a plain final class and NOT a case class - no Mirror, no fromProduct - obtainable only from the certifying pseudonymization path. So raw text cannot be placed in a forged request and THE RAW-TEXT GUARANTEE HOLDS.

WHAT ACTUALLY FAILS is the POLICY ENVELOPE. A forged request bypasses RemotePolicy.evaluate, and RemoteCapability is forgeable all the way down - it is a case class, as are ProviderFingerprint, ReceiptDigest.Keyed and SensitiveDigest beneath it. So legitimately-pseudonymized text can be sent to a provider off the allowlist, under an expired capability, beyond budget, against an unauthorised model identity, with a payload digest that does not bind the payload. Serious authorization defect; not a raw-text leak.

THE RE-RANK STANDS on the corrected reason: a forgeable authorization envelope still outranks arithmetic corruption.

HOW THE ERROR WAS MADE, recorded so it is not repeated: the chief read the Scaladoc promise, confirmed the type was forgeable, and inferred the promise was false, without checking whether the SPECIFIC CONTENT of that promise survived the forge. A forgeable type loses the guarantees that depend on CONSTRUCTION; this one depended on the payload's type instead.

OUTSTANDING: CheckedSidecarPrelude, Credence and Coverage were assessed the same shallow way and must be re-verified at this depth before slice authors rely on the ranking.
